title: Effects of frequency and duration of training on attrition and incidence of injury
authors: Pollock ML, Gettman LR, Milesis CA, Bah MD, Durstine L, Johnson RB
population: 157 male prison inmates aged 20 to 35 y, 20-week jogging programme at 85 to 90% of maximum HR
findings: Subjects were randomly assigned to a control or exercise group: 87 male state-prison inmates trained 3 days a week for 15, 30 or 45 min, and 70 county-jail inmates trained 30 min for 1, 3 or 5 days a week, for 20 weeks at 85 to 90% of maximum heart rate.
Injury occurred in 22%, 24% and 54% of the 15, 30 and 45 min duration groups, and in 0%, 12% and 39% of the 1, 3 and 5 day per week groups.

Attrition from injury was 0%, 0% and 17% (duration groups) and 0%, 4% and 6% (frequency groups); attrition from lack of interest was similar in all training groups (25%) and significantly lower in controls (10%).

Fitness improved in direct proportion to frequency and duration, but the 45 min and 5 days per week programmes are not recommended for beginning joggers because of the significantly greater injury rate.
limitations: Young male prisoners, continuous jogging at a hard 85-90% HRmax (not an easy novice pace), 1970s footwear and surfaces, small arms; no run-walk arm; durations tested were 15, 30 and 45 min, so 20 min was not tested.
implications: At 3 sessions a week, 15 and 30 min sessions had similar injury rates (22% vs 24%) while 45 min had 54%; this supports 30 min as the ceiling for a starting block and 45 min as too much, but says nothing specific about 20 min.
Three days a week (12% injury) is a sensible start frequency; 5 days (39%) is not for beginners.
Because intensity was high (85-90% HRmax), do not carry these rates across to an easy-paced plan; use as direction only, grade C.

verification.notes: Crossref resolves 10.1249/00005768-197721000-00005 (MSSE, first author Pollock, 1977); Europe PMC DOI search did not return it, so the abstract was fetched by PMID 870782 (EXT_ID) and all percentages and group sizes match. Corrected the garbled first finding (it contained a stray '30 min sessions? no:') and removed the claim that 3 x 20 to 3 x 30 is defensible, since 20 min was not tested.
